title: Govt caps margin at 30 pc of MRP on non-scheduled cancer drugs; patients may save Rs 2,500 crore annually
excerpt: New Delhi, October 9 (IANS): The government has expanded price controls on cancer medicines to curb excessive pricing and reduce out-of-pocket expenses for patients, according to an official statement. The Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilisers said it caps margins on the supply and sale of non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs at 30 per cent of the Maximum Retail Price (MRP).The decision is expected to reduce prices by up to 70 per cent and help cancer patients save Rs 2,500 crore annually, it added. Moreover, essential cancer medicines in the scheduled list are already subject to government-set ceiling prices. The new decision extends protection to non-scheduled cancer medicines outside that list by limiting margins added before they reach patients. An expert committee under the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) will finalise list of medicines to be covered and the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) will then issue a notification, the government said. It further noted that cancer incidence is rising in India with approximately 60 people per one lakh population affected saying that NPPA’s analysis found non-scheduled anti-cancer medicines carry average mark-up of about 170 per cent, reaching 700 per cent or more in some cases with prices varying sharply between retail pharmacy, hospital pharmacy and online channels. In addition, state authorities in Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Karnataka along with patients and civil society had raised concerns over excessive prices and large gap between purchase price and MRP.The intervention builds on the 2019 decision when NPPA capped trade margins on 42 selected non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs under DPCO, 2013 which reduced MRPs by up to 91 per cent with reported annual savings of Rs 984 crore across 526 brands, the government said. To ensure availability, manufacturers will be required to maintain current production levels. Also, the cap will cover branded and generic, domestically produced and imported, patented and non-patented, non-scheduled anti-cancer medicines.

title: WTITC calls for balanced approach to US suspension of PERM processing
excerpt: HYDERABAD: World Telugu Information Technology Council (WTITC) has called for a balanced and constructive approach to the U.S. government’s decision to suspend PERM (Permanent Labour Certification) processing for eight major technology companies. Sundeep Kumar Makthala, Chairman of WTITC, said the development highlights the need to balance national employment priorities, regulatory compliance, and global talent mobility […]HYDERABAD: World Telugu Information Technology Council (WTITC) has called for a balanced and constructive approach to the U.S. government's decision to suspend PERM (Permanent Labour Certification) processing for eight major technology companies. Sundeep Kumar Makthala, Chairman of WTITC, said the development highlights the need to balance national employment priorities, regulatory compliance, and global talent mobility in an increasingly interconnected technology sector. He explained, “Every country has the right to protect its workforce and enforce its immigration laws. At the same time, the technology sector thrives on global talent, innovation, and cross-border collaboration. The objective should be to ensure that domestic labour market needs and international talent mobility complement each other.” Furthermore, he noted that PERM is a critical stage in many employer-sponsored lawful permanent residency (Green Card) applications. He clarified that the suspension may create uncertainty for affected foreign national professionals, but does not result in the automatic revocation of existing H-1B visas or the termination of all employment for current employees. Global talent mobility Moreover, emphasising the global nature of the technology industry, Makthala said the United States remains a key center for technology, research, and investment, while India continues to strengthen its position as a global innovation and talent hub. He added that concerns over immigration program compliance should be addressed through transparent, evidence-based audits and investigations, without generalizing allegations against individual employers to the broader industry or skilled workforce. In addition, the development, he said, is also relevant to Telugu professionals from Telangana and Andhra Pradesh who contribute to international technology and entrepreneurial ecosystems. WTITC, which connects 2,843 member companies across 63 countries, remains committed to promoting international business partnerships and technology collaboration. Makthala emphasised that India should continue strengthening its capabilities in artificial intelligence, semiconductors, advanced engineering, and scientific research, while maintaining constructive engagement with the United States and other global technology markets. “Our goal should be to build strong technology ecosystems domestically while creating opportunities through responsible global partnerships. Fair employment practices, predictable regulatory frameworks, and international cooperation can benefit businesses, professionals, and national economies worldwide,” he said. ]]>

title: India partners as pilot country with ITU to bridge AI gap for Global South
excerpt: Communications Minister Jyotiraditya M. Scindia said on Friday that ultimately, the true measure of artificial intelligence (AI) will not be the size of its models or the sophistication of its algorithms, but the number of human lives it improves.â€œThe journey of the AI for Good Lab from Geneva to New Delhi mirrors the journey that artificial intelligence itself must make -- from global conversations to local solutions, from technological possibility to human impact, and from strategy to scale. The distance between AI ambition and AI impact is bridged by skills, compute, data, institutions, and connectivity," the minister said in his address at the inauguration of the "AI for Good Lab Workshop: From Strategy to Impact," at the India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026, organised jointly by the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) and the International Telecommunication Union (ITU).As one of the ten pilot countries alongside partners from Africa, Asia, Latin America, and the Gulf, India brings its model of shared compute, open datasets, and Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) to lead cross-regional learning and technical collaboration across the Global South. The sessions at the workshop delivered structured deliberation on defining a concrete roadmap for institutional engagement, priority sector adoption, and Global South knowledge-sharing. Stakeholders achieved a shared understanding of the AI Sandbox requirements to support experimentation while validating fairness, robustness, and safety before scaling solutions to the last citizen. Scindia reiterated India's guiding philosophy of "Sarvajan Hitaya, Sarvajan Sukhaya" (for the welfare of all, for the happiness of all), noting that while nearly 2.2 billion people worldwide remain offline, technology must expand human opportunity rather than concentrate it, ensuring the digital divide does not morph into an AI divide. He detailed key milestones driving India's domestic AI capabilities and digital infrastructure under the Rs 10,000-crore-plus IndiaAI Mission. On the compute infrastructure front, more than 38,000 high-end GPUs have been onboarded at approximately one-third of the global average cost, with an additional 20,000 GPUs being added. In terms of open data and talent, the AI Kosh platform is unlocking datasets and sovereign models across agriculture, healthcare, and education. India currently ranks first globally in relative AI skill penetration, with Indian developers contributing approximately 5.2 per cent of open-source AI projects on GitHub with ten or more stars. Furthermore, telecom innovation is being paired with trust through AI and data analytics tools like Sanchar Saathi, which has facilitated the disconnection of over 7.14 crore fraudulent mobile connections, traced over 35 lakh lost handsets, and prevented potential financial fraud worth over Rs 5,000 crore. To support standardisation, India's Telecommunication Engineering Centre (TEC) has developed national standards covering AI fairness, robustness, and incident reporting, while establishing a National Working Group on AI Standardisation to align with ITU-T global benchmarks, the minister observed. Key international dignitaries, including Bilel Jamoussi, Deputy Director of the ITU Telecommunication Standardisation Bureau, Amit Agrawal, Secretary, Department of Telecommunications, along with distinguished researchers, innovators, industry leaders, and policy experts, participated in the discussions.

title: Gujarat offers MSMEs interest aid, power subsidies and support for AI adoption
excerpt: The Gujarat government has introduced a five-year incentive scheme for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), offering assistance for capital investment, interest payments, electricity costs, employee provident fund contributions and technology adoption, including artificial intelligence (AI), under its 'Viksit Gujarat Industrial Policy-2026'.Announced by the Industries and Mines Department under the leadership of Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel and Deputy Chief Minister Harsh Sanghavi, the Assistance Scheme for MSMEs came into effect on June 1, 2026. It will remain operational until May 31, 2031. The scheme provides for a combination of incentives, with the maximum cumulative assistance capped at 45 per cent of eligible fixed capital investment (EFCI) in Category-A talukas and 35 per cent in Category-B areas. For identified thrust sectors, the limits have been increased to 50 per cent and 45 per cent, respectively. Under the scheme, eligible enterprises can receive interest assistance of seven per cent on term loans for five years, along with electricity tariff assistance of up to Rs 2 per unit in Category-A areas and Rs 1 per unit in Category-B areas for the same period. Capital investment assistance in Category-A areas will be up to 35 per cent of eligible investment for micro enterprises, calculated based on expenditure disbursed in one year, and up to 35 per cent for small and medium enterprises over five years. The corresponding rate in Category-B areas will be 25 per cent. Women entrepreneurs, registered manufacturing startups and first-generation entrepreneurs will be eligible for an additional one percentage point of interest assistance, within the prescribed limits. Micro enterprises will receive higher annual incentive limits during their initial years. In Category-A areas, the limit will be up to 37 per cent in the first year, while in Category-B areas it will be up to 27 per cent. The annual limit in subsequent years will be two per cent for both categories, with more favourable provisions for micro enterprises in identified thrust sectors. To encourage employment generation, the scheme provides for reimbursement of up to 100 per cent of the employer's Employees' Provident Fund (EPF) contribution for newly recruited employees for five years. The monthly reimbursement will be capped at the lower of 12 per cent of the employee's basic salary, dearness allowance and retaining allowance, or Rs 1,800 for male employees, Rs 2,500 for female employees and Rs 3,000 for employees with disabilities. Additional employment generated through expansion or diversification will also qualify. The government has also earmarked assistance for quality certification, digital systems and technology acquisition. Enterprises installing enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems will be eligible for assistance covering 65 per cent of capital expenditure, up to Rs 1 lakh. For national and international quality certification, assistance of up to 50 per cent of certification fees and the cost of necessary testing equipment and machinery will be available, subject to a ceiling of Rs 10 lakh. Assistance of up to Rs 50,000 will be provided for Zero Defect, Zero Effect (ZED) certification, covering up to 50 per cent of the charges remaining after central government assistance. For information and communication technology infrastructure supporting Industry 4.0 and AI-based systems, eligible enterprises can receive up to 65 per cent of capital expenditure, capped at Rs 5 lakh. Technology acquired from recognised institutions will attract assistance of up to 65 per cent, capped at Rs 50 lakh for general MSMEs and Rs 1 crore for enterprises in identified thrust sectors. Patent registration will qualify for assistance of up to 75 per cent of expenditure, capped at Rs 25 lakh per applicant or enterprise. In identified thrust sectors, support of up to 75 per cent, capped at Rs 1 crore, will cover intellectual property rights, including patents, designs, copyrights, trademarks and geographical indication registrations. Micro enterprises and artisans in these sectors will also be eligible for reimbursement of up to 80 per cent of AI subscription fees, capped at Rs 1 lakh annually for three years. For energy and water conservation, the scheme provides assistance of up to 75 per cent of the audit cost, capped at Rs 50,000 for each audit. A one-time subsidy covering up to 25 per cent of the cost of equipment recommended by the auditor, capped at Rs 20 lakh, will also be available, subject to a minimum 10 per cent saving in energy or water consumption against the average monthly consumption recorded over the preceding 12 months.MSMEs raising equity through an SME exchange under Securities and Exchange Board of India guidelines can receive one-time assistance covering up to 25 per cent of fundraising expenditure, capped at Rs 5 lakh. Enterprises obtaining collateral-free term loans under the Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE) framework will be eligible for reimbursement of up to 100 per cent of the annual service fee for five years. Additional assistance will be available for eligible enterprises outside Gujarat Industrial Development Corporation (GIDC) estates or approved industrial parks. The scheme provides for reimbursement of up to 35 per cent of charges paid to a distribution licensee for a new electricity connection, additional load or alteration of a connection or service line, capped at Rs 5 lakh.MSMEs renting or leasing industrial sheds for manufacturing can receive assistance covering up to 65 per cent of rent paid, while enterprises wholly owned by women will be eligible for up to 75 per cent, subject to a maximum of Rs 3 lakh annually for five years. Identified thrust sectors include sports equipment, toys, footwear, robots and drones. Eligible enterprises in these sectors will receive 100 per cent reimbursement of stamp duty and registration charges paid on the purchase or lease of land. The package also provides for reimbursement of international certification fees up to Rs 5 crore, employee training assistance of up to Rs 8,000 per employee per month during the first 12 months, and support covering up to 50 per cent of the cost of establishing a creative design studio, capped at Rs 5 crore. Enterprises availing benefits under the scheme must employ at least 85 per cent of their total workforce from among Gujarat residents. At least 60 per cent of employees at managerial and supervisory levels must also be residents of the state. The scheme allows eligible asset purchases and payments made from January 1, 2026, to be considered, subject to prescribed conditions. The eligible investment period will be 12 months from the Date of Commercial Production (DoCP) for plant and machinery investments of up to Rs 50 crore, and 18 months for investments exceeding Rs 50 crore and up to Rs 125 crore.

The package also provides for reimbursement of international certification fees up to Rs 5 crore, employee training assistance of up to Rs 8,000 per employee per month during the first 12 months, and support covering up to 50 per cent of the cost of establishing a creative design studio, capped at Rs 5 crore. Enterprises availing benefits under the scheme must employ at least 85 per cent of their total workforce from among Gujarat residents. At least 60 per cent of employees at managerial and supervisory levels must also be residents of the state. The scheme allows eligible asset purchases and payments made from January 1, 2026, to be considered, subject to prescribed conditions. The eligible investment period will be 12 months from the Date of Commercial Production (DoCP) for plant and machinery investments of up to Rs 50 crore, and 18 months for investments exceeding Rs 50 crore and up to Rs 125 crore. --IANS mys/dan

title: BIZVERSE’26 Brings 460 Participants to JK Lakshmipat University, Jaipur
excerpt: JK Lakshmipat University (JKLU), Jaipur, successfully concluded BIZVERSE’26, its two-day national management fest, held on 5–6 October 2026. The inaugural edition attracted 460 unique participants representing 115 teams, establishing BIZVERSE’26 as a vibrant platform for experiential learning and real-world problem-solving through creativity, technology and competition. The fest attracted participation from institutions spread across several states, including Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Delhi-NCR and Uttar Pradesh. A notable feature of BIZVERSE’26 was its multidisciplinary participation. The inaugural ceremony was graced by Mr. Saurabh Khandelwal, Founder and CEO, DGS Translogistics India Pvt. Ltd., as Chief Guest. Speaking on “From Small-Town Dreams to a Pan-India Enterprise,” he encouraged students to combine ambition with determination and entrepreneurial thinking. Delivering the inaugural address, Dr. Vijaysekhar Chellaboina, Vice-Chancellor, JKLU, said,” “BIZVERSE’26 reflects JKLU’s commitment to creating learning experiences that extend beyond the classroom. By bringing together students from diverse disciplines and institutions, the fest encouraged them to apply knowledge, embrace technology, think creatively and solve real-world business challenges.” Dr. Sheetal Mundra, Acting Head of JKLU’s Institute of Management, stressed that a platform like BIZVERSE plays a vital role in preparing young people to navigate an increasingly dynamic and interconnected world with confidence. The two-day fest featured six major competitions -- Biz Quiz, Biz Reel, Meme Marketing, Prompt Battle, Biz Lab and Case Cracker -- centred on business awareness, creativity, artificial intelligence, strategic thinking, decision-making and problem-solving. Open Business Games and two panel discussions titled “Beyond the Classroom: Making Campus Life Count” and “Future Ready: Skills, Mindset and Careers in a Changing World” further enriched the experience. The competitive results reflected the strong participation of institutions from outside JKLU. Jaipuria Institute of Management Jaipur emerged winner of Meme Marketing, represented by Sanya Goyal, Siya Nowal, Sneha Methi and Tanvi Agarwal, while Poornima University claimed the top position in Prompt Battle, with Prasham Jain, Lakshay Varshney and Vikas Bagla. Vivekananda Global University (VGU) secured the runner-up position in Biz Lab, while Mandsaur University, Madhya Pradesh, finished runner-up in Biz Reel, underlining the competitive strength and inter-institutional character of the fest. JKLU teams also delivered strong performances across the competitions. Shrey Rawat, Romit Gandhi, Vishal Bansal and Ashutosh Gupta won Biz Lab; Aman Jhanjharia, Aahan and Anijsht Amitanshu won Biz Quiz; Nimit Jain, Pranav Gurjar, Akshat Garg and Lavish Kumawat emerged winners of Biz Reel; while Rashi Lunawat, Esha Bafna and Rashi Loya secured the top position in Case Cracker. The fest concluded with a valedictory session graced by Dr. Shrikant Baldi, IAS (Retd.), Former Chief Secretary, Himachal Pradesh, as Chief Guest. BIZVERSE’26 concluded as a celebration of experiential learning and inter-institutional engagement, bringing together business, technology, creativity and young talent on a common platform to Think, Strategize, Compete and Lead.

title: Maha govt advances 'Quantum City' plans with London tech, investment mission
excerpt: A high-level delegation from the Government of Maharashtra concluded a strategic two-day quantum, artificial intelligence (AI), and investment mission to London on October 7 and 8. The initiative aims to position Maharashtra as India's premier quantum and AI capital by laying the groundwork for a "Quantum City" and a UK-Maharashtra "Quantum Corridor".Organised and facilitated by the Global India Business Corridor (GIBC UK), the mission provided Maharashtra a prominent platform at The City Quantum & AI Summit. The state delegation comprised Industries Department Principal Secretary P. Anbalagan and Chief Investment Advisor to Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, Kaustubh Dhavse. During the mission, delegates held 13 bilateral meetings with global CEOs, investors and public institution leaders to attract advanced deep-tech operations and capital to Maharashtra. Key proposals and technical initiatives discussed during the bilateral meetings included a Mumbai quantum facility, research and AI infrastructure, infrastructure and security solutions, industrial and governance applications, and workforce and start-up support. The mission focuses on establishing a dedicated quantum computing hub in Mumbai, building an AI engineering and research base alongside sustainable, energy-efficient data centres, implementing quantum sensing tools for safer underground transport construction, and deploying advanced cyber security systems for critical infrastructure. It also aims to deploy AI systems to streamline investor approvals, establish advanced manufacturing centres to help micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) integrate into global supply chains, and implement targeted workforce training programmes and incubation support for technology start-ups. In addition, discussions with representatives of the City of London Corporation explored creating an institutional finance channel between London and Mumbai to fund large-scale infrastructure developments in Maharashtra. An illustrative GIBC planning scenario estimates that, if proposed projects secure formal funding and reach operational maturity, the initiative could generate approximately Rs 20,000 crore in cumulative economic activity over a 10-year horizon. This figure encompasses investments, operational expenditure and broader economic spillover effects, with the potential to create up to 8,000 direct and supported jobs. However, GIBC noted that these estimates remain illustrative planning projections and do not currently represent committed capital or confirmed hiring. If fully realised, the corridor is expected to provide local engineers, researchers and entrepreneurs with expanded global access while enhancing Maharashtra's technological capabilities, administrative efficiency and critical infrastructure resilience, government sources said.

title: 'Act of dishonesty': Maha Minister slams Rahul Gandhi for 'supporting' Elon Musk
excerpt: Maharashtra Cultural Affairs, Electronics, Information Technology and Artificial Intelligence Development Minister Ashish Shelar on Friday said that favouring an American industrialist amounted to "dishonesty" on the part of Leader of the Opposition (LoP) in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi. Mumbai, Oct 9 (IANS) Maharashtra Cultural Affairs, Electronics, Information Technology and Artificial Intelligence Development Minister Ashish Shelar on Friday said that favouring an American industrialist amounted to "dishonesty" on the part of Leader of the Opposition (LoP) in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi. He also remarked that the ongoing protests by the Opposition against the SIR process amounted to the "grammar of anarchy".Speaking to reporters about LoP in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi criticising the Indian government while supporting remarks made by Elon Musk, Shelar said the matter concerned the Central Government. However, he added that Rahul Gandhi's defence of the businessman in question amounted to dishonesty. He said that the United States was imposing restrictions affecting Indian technology companies and that such developments were not conducive to the careers and employment prospects of young Indians working there. According to Shelar, supporting an American company at such a time amounted to dishonesty. The Minister further said that officials had already clarified that work on the security verification framework concerning Elon Musk and Starlink was underway. He said the Central Government or the concerned authorities would take an appropriate decision on the matter. However, he alleged that Rahul Gandhi had chosen to side with reactions coming from the United States without waiting for that decision, which, according to him, amounted to dishonesty towards India's administrative system. On the Opposition's ongoing protests in Delhi, Shelar said such demonstrations questioned the country's institutions and amounted to the "grammar of anarchy".He said there was an opportunity to raise such issues in the Lok Sabha and that the constitutional platform existed to discuss all concerns. According to him, instead of debating the matter in the House, Opposition leaders were choosing to protest outside. Criticising Abhijit Dipke's reported statement that an Emergency had been imposed in the country, Shelar said Dipke's understanding of civics appeared weak."If Abhijit Dipke believes that an Emergency has been imposed in the country, he clearly does not understand what an Emergency means," Shelar said. He argued that Dipke should ask the Congress about the Emergency period and whether people were free to speak and write during that time. He also criticised the CJP protest, describing it as an attempt to outmanoeuvre the Congress politically.
